findings.text: Per-CPU masking operates on one of two enable words chosen by position relative to a fixed split, affecting a single bit, and orders the update with a synchronization barrier so both disable and enable become visible promptly in support of lazy disable.

Shared and message interrupts are disabled and enabled through fabric commands combining identity with category; disable adds a completion barrier for prompt effect while enable relies on finite-time completion alone.
Completion signaling combines identity with category; per-CPU completions are omitted when the descriptor is marked forwarded to a virtual CPU, while shared and message completions always issue.

Affinity programming resolves a single target CPU under forced versus online-constrained policy, converts it to fabric affinity, issues a binding command, then publishes the chosen CPU as effective and reports handled.
A small selector distinguishes pending, active and handling-mode views of per-CPU state, with low and high register pairs and separate set and clear paths for mutable views.

Per-CPU state observation masks the chosen view for pending or active and rejects other queries; shared and message observation probes configuration then samples status after ordering with rejection on an invalid flag, while mutation for those categories is pending-only.

Retrigger for shared and message interrupts is expressed as asserting pending with success mapped to a positive result; inter-processor signaling marks the underlying message interrupt pending via hierarchy retrigger.
Per-CPU trigger mode is immutable; a type request is checked against the hardware handling-mode report and rejected on edge versus level mismatch, otherwise accepted without hardware change.
Virtual CPU attachment toggles a forwarded marker on the descriptor, set when an owner is supplied and cleared otherwise, always reporting success.

Four chip descriptors partition behavior: per-CPU covers masking, completion, type validation, state and virtual affinity; shared adds affinity and retrigger with masked-type and pre-startup affinity traits; message covers affinity and retrigger without type; inter-processor delegates masking, completion, affinity and state to its parent and adds single-target send; all share suspend and wake traits.

Domain operation tables bind translation plus reservation plus release plus matching for per-CPU and shared, reservation plus release only for message, and layered reservation plus release for inter-processor.

Firmware translation validates container kind and cell count with category matching the target domain, extracts identity and trigger, then derives per-CPU type from hardware mode while shared type comes from sense bits.
Per-CPU and shared domain matching each require firmware node equality plus category agreement plus identity with the corresponding registered global domain.

Per-CPU reservation allows exactly one interrupt, translates, flags level lines, designates percpu-device handling and installs percpu-device dispatch; release clears the handler and resets the descriptor.

Shared reservation allows exactly one, translates, binds interconnect chip data by identity, installs fast completion dispatch, marks probe and single-target, and initializes hardware at middle priority.

Message interrupts reset to edge handling with pending cleared; reservation iterates the requested count with two-stage booking and unwinds prior successes on any failure while installing fast dispatch with single-target and middle priority; release walks the range releasing identifiers and resetting descriptors.

Inter-processor reservation first allocates through the parent then assigns sequential local identities with single-target marking and percpu dispatch; release clears handlers and resets descriptors then frees through the parent, stopping early if a descriptor is missing.

Exception entry samples activation and exits when invalid, otherwise orders activation with acknowledge and instruction barriers, issues an early priority release to permit nesting or guest entry, then dispatches the decoded interrupt to its categorical domain with explicit completion if dispatch fails.
Categorical dispatch routes to per-CPU, shared or message domains; unknown categories log once and stop, and undispatchable identities log once then complete explicitly.
CPU interface enable starts from cleared per-CPU enables, establishes per-CPU priorities and a middle threshold, then sets global enable; disable clears global enable and orders with a barrier.

Per-CPU start validates the interface feature, enables the interface, then registers the CPU with the interconnect; multiprocessor init registers the starting hook and allocates one contiguous inter-processor range sized by per-CPU count times CPU count, publishing it when allocation succeeds.
The integration surface comprises an exception entry, hotplug and init entries, per-category domain vectors and per-category chip vectors for masking, completion, affinity, state and retrigger.

Invalid probe status, unknown category, undispatchable identity, identifier or table exhaustion with unwind, affinity translation failure, trigger mismatch, multi-request misuse, missing CPU feature and inter-processor range exhaustion are signaled via error returns, warnings or one-time logs, with explicit completion on undispatchable interrupts.
Per-CPU register selection splits at number sixty-four, with low and high words each covering sixty-four positions addressed by number modulo sixty-four.
Three hardware categories distinguish per-CPU, shared and message interrupts across fabric commands, dispatch routing, translation and domain matching.
A middle priority level serves as the default for hardware initialization and CPU threshold programming.
Total inter-processor reservation equals per-CPU count multiplied by configured CPU count in one contiguous range.
